svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "One cardiac cycle (about 0.8 s): pressures, volume, ECG and heart sounds, left side of the heart."], [1.0, "Atrial systole (after the P wave): the atrium tops up the ventricle."], [2.95, "QRS: the ventricle contracts. Ventricular pressure exceeds atrial pressure, the AV valve closes: first heart sound."], [3.1125000000000003, "Isovolumetric contraction: all valves closed, pressure rises, volume unchanged."], [3.7624999999999997, "Ventricular pressure exceeds aortic pressure (about 80 mmHg): the aortic valve opens; ejection."], [7.824999999999999, "Ventricular pressure falls below aortic: the aortic valve closes (second heart sound, dicrotic notch)."], [7.9875, "Isovolumetric relaxation: all valves closed again."], [9.125, "Ventricular pressure falls below atrial: the AV valve opens and the ventricle fills."]]
svg.title: The cardiac cycle (Wiggers diagram)
svg.desc: A Wiggers diagram of one cardiac cycle: aortic, left ventricular and left atrial pressures, ventricular volume, ECG and heart sounds, with valve opening and closing points and the phases of the cycle.
svg.text: Left side of the heart, about 75 beats per minute. Typical resting values.

g.data-info: Atrial systole → isovolumetric contraction → ejection → isovolumetric relaxation → ventricular filling.
Aortic pressure (red), left ventricular pressure (blue) and left atrial pressure (green), in mmHg.
About 120 ml at the end of diastole and 50 ml at the end of systole: stroke volume about 70 ml.
P wave: atria depolarise. QRS: ventricles depolarise. T wave: ventricles repolarise.
“Lub” (S1): AV valves close at the start of ventricular systole. “Dub” (S2): semilunar valves close at the end.
A valve opens when the pressure behind it is higher than the pressure in front of it, and closes when the pressure difference reverses.
